title: Expressing the sense of the House of Representatives that Congress must refuse to provide any additional funds or exceptional regulatory support to companies or financial institutions facing insolvency or financial collapse due to exposures to acute stress within the artificial intelligence market and must provide support to all harmed Americans instead.
action: Referred to the Committee on Financial Services, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The House says Congress should not give extra money or special rules to companies or banks that are in trouble because of AI market problems. Instead, Congress must focus on helping the American people who have been hurt by these issues.

title: Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026 is a U.S. law that sets out standards and oversight for the development of trustworthy AI systems, emphasizing safety, transparency, and accountability. It requires research institutions to meet these criteria and establishes a federal agency to monitor and enforce compliance.

title: VA AI Transparency Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations.
summary: The VA AI Transparency Act of 2026 seeks to make the use of artificial intelligence within the Veterans Affairs system more open and understandable. It requires the VA to share information about AI algorithms, data sources, and how decisions are made so that veterans and the public can hold the system accountable.

title: VA Claims AI Accountability Act
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations.
summary: The VA Claims AI Accountability Act seeks to establish clear rules for the use of artificial intelligence in processing veterans' claims, ensuring that these systems are reliable, transparent, and fair. The law aims to protect veterans' rights by mandating oversight, accountability, and safeguards against bias or errors in AI-driven decisions.

title: Securing Elections From AI Deception Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The Securing Elections From AI Deception Act aims to protect electoral processes by regulating the use of artificial intelligence tools that could spread misinformation. It sets requirements for transparency, verification, and penalties for parties that deploy deceptive AI content during elections.

title: Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act aims to safeguard shoppers from misleading or false AI-generated content. It establishes standards and penalties to ensure transparency and honesty in AI communications.

title: Advanced AI Security Readiness Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select).
summary: The Advanced AI Security Readiness Act proposes new rules to make sure artificial‑intelligence systems are secure and reliable before they are released to the public. It would set testing standards, encourage developers to follow best practices, and create guidelines to reduce potential risks from advanced AI.

title: CISA Securing AI Task Force Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The CISA Securing AI Task Force Act establishes a federal task force to oversee the security of artificial intelligence systems, ensuring they are protected against cyber threats and misuse. It aims to create standards, guidelines, and collaboration among government, industry, and academia to promote safe and trustworthy AI deployment.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026 aims to establish a national framework for identifying, assessing, and mitigating risks associated with AI technologies. It requires organizations to implement robust security measures, conduct regular risk assessments, and report AI-related incidents to ensure public safety and trust.

title: Artificial Intelligence Physical Systems Coordination Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Physical Systems Coordination Act of 2026 establishes regulations and guidelines for the development, deployment, and oversight of AI-powered physical systems, aiming to ensure safety, accountability, and public trust. It outlines responsibilities for manufacturers, operators, and government agencies to coordinate efforts, share data, and enforce standards to mitigate risks associated with autonomous and semi-autonomous technologies.

title: Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on House Administration.
summary: The Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act is legislation designed to safeguard the integrity of elections by regulating the use of artificial intelligence in political contexts. It aims to prevent deceptive AI‑generated content from misleading voters and to enforce transparency and accountability in AI‑driven political messaging.

title: Self-Improving AI Monitoring Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The Self‑Improving AI Monitoring Act proposes rules to keep AI systems that can modify themselves under close oversight, ensuring they operate safely and transparently. It likely sets up monitoring frameworks, reporting standards, and safety checks for developers and users of self‑improving AI technologies.

title: Stop Rogue AI Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop Rogue AI Act is a proposed law that aims to prevent the creation and use of artificial intelligence systems that could act independently and cause harm. It would establish strict rules, oversight, and penalties to keep AI development under human control and ensure it follows safety and ethical standards.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act proposes to temporarily halt the construction and operation of new data centers that are dedicated to artificial intelligence. This pause is intended to curb environmental impacts, manage resource consumption, and give lawmakers time to develop more efficient policies for AI infrastructure.

title: Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations Act of 2026 creates a federal board tasked with examining and addressing cybersecurity incidents that involve artificial intelligence. The board will investigate, report on, and recommend policies to protect national digital infrastructure from AI-driven threats.

title: Make AI Work for Americans Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
summary: The Make AI Work for Americans Act is a legislative proposal that aims to ensure artificial intelligence technology benefits U.S. citizens by encouraging responsible innovation and supporting workforce development. It seeks to establish policies that promote ethical AI use, protect privacy, and create opportunities for Americans to gain skills and jobs in the AI economy.

title: China AI Power Report Act
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 47 - 0.
summary: The China AI Power Report Act requires companies that develop or use artificial intelligence in China to submit detailed reports on the computing hardware and energy consumption of their AI systems. This law aims to increase transparency, promote energy efficiency, and ensure that AI infrastructure complies with national security and environmental standards.

title: Doctors Not AI Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on Ways and Means, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Doctors Not AI Act of 2026 aims to limit the use of artificial intelligence in medical practice, ensuring that only licensed human doctors can provide diagnoses and treatment plans. It seeks to protect patient safety and maintain professional accountability by restricting AI involvement in direct patient care.

title: To establish the Office of Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology Threats within the Executive Office of the President, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The bill would create a new Office of Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology Threats in the President’s Executive Office to coordinate monitoring, risk assessment, and response to AI and other emerging technology challenges. It also includes related measures to strengthen national security, protect the workforce, and support the economy.

title: A resolution establishing the Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence.
action: Referred to the Committee on Rules and Administration. (text: CR S5172-5174)
summary: The resolution establishes a Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence to oversee and guide AI policy and regulation. The committee will evaluate AI’s impacts, propose regulatory measures, and help shape national strategies for responsible AI use.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025
action: Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs. Hearings held.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025 establishes a formal process for assessing the potential hazards of AI systems before they are released or used in critical applications. It requires developers and organizations to conduct risk analyses, report findings to a designated regulatory body, and comply with guidelines designed to mitigate negative impacts on safety, privacy, and society.

title: CREATE AI Act of 2025
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 29 - 0.
summary: The CREATE AI Act of 2025 is a proposed set of regulations designed to govern how artificial intelligence is developed, deployed, and used in the United States. It emphasizes transparency, safety, and accountability, setting guidelines to ensure AI systems are developed responsibly and benefit society.

title: Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026 is a law that requires developers and users of AI systems to evaluate and reduce their environmental footprints, such as energy use and carbon emissions. It sets clear guidelines for reporting these impacts, promotes greener AI technologies, and imposes penalties for non‑compliance.
